correctness.rationale: Prefix normality compares, for each attainable number of ones, the least span of any consecutive ones with their first prefix occurrence. Thus it is exactly the gap-window test in the record. The two exceptional gaps are at indices a and a+c. At window size a the middle and last one-run cannot contain an all-unit window, giving a>=max(c,e). For sizes a through a+c-1 an alternative can have only the second exceptional gap precisely when c+e-1>=a for some such size, in which case size a already witnesses the required d>=b; for sizes at least a+c both gaps are forced. The terminal zeros do not affect any of these spans. The disjoint enumeration, rational simplification and dominant-pole coefficient at z=1 give the stated bivariate function and 7/24 proportion against binom(n,5). Direct independent finite membership and GF coefficient checks agreed at every (n,m) through n=12, including totals 1,3,10,23,50,94,169,280. Replay by directly counting ones in every factor of each three-one-run word of length at most 12, and multiplying truncated inverse-denominator series in the two markers. This is bounded corroboration only; the gap and GF arguments give the infinite identity. The supplied script was inspected but not executed; the frozen metadata does not record formal verification or expert attestation.
